transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I'm here because I've been really struggling to cope with a traumatic event that happened about two years and three months ago. I am constantly plagued by distressing, intrusive memories and awful nightmares about it that I just can't seem to shake. It has gotten to the point where I really need some help.
Can you tell me more about when these symptoms started and how they've changed over time since the traumatic event occurred?

They started almost right after the event happened, about two years and three months ago. Since then, they haven't really gotten any better and have just remained a constant, distressing part of my daily life.
Do you find yourself avoiding people, places, or activities that remind you of the traumatic event, and if so, how often does this occur?

Yes, I absolutely do. I constantly go out of my way to avoid certain people, places, and activities that might remind me of what happened, almost on a daily basis. I've been doing this for over two years now because facing those reminders causes me way too much distress.
How have these symptoms and avoidance behaviors affected your daily life, relationships, and ability to work or engage in activities you once enjoyed?

I've completely pulled away from my friends and family because I feel so emotionally detached and find it really hard to be close to anyone anymore. I also avoid social gatherings and activities I used to enjoy because they trigger those memories, which has left me feeling totally isolated and like an outsider.
Do you often find yourself on edge, having difficulty relaxing, or being easily startled by small noises or unexpected movements?

Yes, I constantly feel incredibly on edge, tense, and completely unable to relax. My nerves always feel extremely sharp and sensitive, which makes me feel highly reactive to everything in my surroundings.
Have you experienced any significant guilt, shame, or self-blame related to the traumatic event, or do you tend to blame others or circumstances for what happened?

Yes, I carry an overwhelming amount of guilt and shame about what happened. I constantly blame myself and feel deep remorse, always thinking I should have done something differently. I don't blame anyone else or the circumstances—I just feel like it's my fault.

Just to make sure I understand your experience, can you summarize for me how these symptoms of intrusive memories, avoidance, hypervigilance, and guilt have impacted your life since the traumatic event?

For the past two years and three months, these feelings have completely cut me off from everyone, making it impossible to be intimate or close to anyone. I've isolated myself from all social activities and pulled away from my loved ones. I just constantly feel like an outsider who doesn't belong anywhere anymore.
